capitol.name: Capitol Music France
capitol.welcomeTitle: Welcome, <accent>Capitol</accent> teams — the answer before the meeting
capitol.welcomeBody: Your A&R teams open a single app: cumulative and per-platform streams, TikTok signal, contract deadlines, what each artist earns. And your artists finally see what you see.

1.title: Connect the Capitol roster
1.desc: Artists appear from day one with their public streams; statements and contracts, once you share them, calibrate everything.

2.title: Map contracts & rights
2.desc: Options, period ends, recoupments, splits, SACEM: every deadline becomes an alert for the A&R, never a surprise for legal.

3.title: The morning brief, by A&R
3.desc: Roster Pulse: what moved overnight, lead track, top platform, TikTok, gap to claim — before the meeting, not during it.

capitol.firstInsight: “Across the 3 pilot artists, <accent>{gap}</accent> of estimated vs. reported gap on the platforms over the last closed quarter: the claim is ready, and it's the platform being questioned, never the label.”

1.delivery: One app: cumulative, per platform, in euros, with the source of every number

2.delivery: Contractual alerts across the roster: option, period end, unusual clause

3.delivery: CAPITOL × FROM DAY 1 artist portal: estimated earnings, their share, their rights — without calling the label

4.delivery: Estimated vs. reported gap by DSP, claim file ready — the label is the claimant, not the audited party

5.delivery: Wavely: annual studio credit, direct booking by A&R and artists, invoiced through UniPort, controlled sessions

umpg.name: Universal Music Publishing France
umpg.welcomeTitle: Welcome, <accent>Universal Music Publishing</accent> songwriters — your work, in continuous
umpg.welcomeBody: Your royalties arrive 6 to 18 months late. Day One tracks what your songs generate every day, your writer's share, your SACEM statements — and prepares the file that shows your catalog as an asset.

1.title: Connect your songs
1.desc: Your titles, your performers, your splits: public streams arrive from day one; your SACEM and publishing statements, once you import them, calibrate your share.

2.title: Track your writer's share
2.desc: Every day: gross generated by the platforms, publisher's share, writer's share per your splits — as a range, with the source of every number.

3.title: Show your catalog as an asset
3.desc: 24-month history, 12-month forecast, valuation range, your publisher's attestation: the funder's file your bank knows how to read.

umpg.firstInsight: “Across the 3 demo artists, <accent>{gap}</accent> of estimated vs. reported gap on the platforms over the last closed quarter — on songs as on masters, it's the platform being questioned, never the publisher.”

1.promise: 18 months late on their own royalties
1.delivery: Daily estimate of the writer's share, reconciled against every SACEM statement

2.delivery: Splits signed per song, France Rights: expected vs. received, songs to declare

3.delivery: Funder's file: history, forecast, valuation, publisher attestation — for the bank

4.promise: A tool built for masters, never for songs
4.delivery: Song-level view built with you: performers, recordings, platforms, syncs

5.delivery: Deductible as a business expense; deployable by the publisher through a CNM digital-transition program

universal.name: Universal Music France
universal.welcomeTitle: Welcome, <accent>Universal</accent> teams — your artists finally see what you see
universal.welcomeBody: And you see what the platforms don't tell you. In 3 minutes, we connect the roster, map the contracts and deliver the first roster brief.
universal.offer: Pilot on a targeted roster, 90 days

1.title: Connect the Universal catalogue
1.desc: Roster, contracts, half-yearly statements: secure import, role-based permissions (label, team, artist).

2.title: Map contracts & rights
2.desc: Options, recoupments, period ends, splits, SACEM: every deadline becomes an alert, never a surprise.

3.title: Receive the first roster brief
3.desc: The label Pulse, calibrated on your data: growth signals, contractual alerts, DSP gaps to claim.

universal.firstInsight: “Across the 3 pilot artists, <accent>{gap}</accent> of estimated vs. reported gap on the platforms over the last closed quarter. DSP claim file ready.”

1.delivery: Retention, fewer disputes: the artist understands their earnings, continuously

2.delivery: Options, recoupments, period ends: no deadline missed

4.delivery: Recover what the platforms underpay: substantiated claim, never an internal conflict

5.delivery: UNIVERSAL × FROM DAY 1: the artist view, with your logo

believe.name: Believe
believe.welcomeTitle: Welcome among the <accent>Believe artists</accent> on From Day 1
believe.welcomeBody: Ismaël Kané (Believe Music Publishing France) recommended the tool to you. In 3 minutes, we import your Believe catalogue and deliver your first strategic report.

1.title: Connect your Believe account
1.desc: 1-click OAuth. We automatically import your distributed tracks, your splits, your 12-month revenue.

2.title: Check your splits and FR rights
2.desc: We detect your co-writers and offer a sync with Sentric / Believe Music Publishing for your publishing.

3.title: Receive your first Pulse
3.desc: The daily strategic brief calibrated on your Believe data. Concrete action #1 to take today.

believe.firstInsight: “We detected <accent>{gap}</accent> to recover on your latest statements (Spotify underpayment). Audit letter ready to send.”

1.delivery: Intelligence + FR rights + AI audit as an upsell

4.delivery: Believe logo in the header, “Believe Artist” badge

direct.name: From Day 1
direct.welcomeBody: Import your distributor statement, we deliver your first brief in 3 minutes.

1.title: Import your statement
1.desc: DistroKid, TuneCore, Believe: one CSV, 100% local.

2.title: Check your tracks and splits
2.desc: We recognise your tracks and suggest the splits to sign.

3.title: Receive your first Pulse
3.desc: Streams, estimated earnings, gaps to claim.

direct.firstInsight: “Your first brief is ready: <accent>{gap}</accent> of gap detected on your latest statement.”
